english: Let $P$ be a point on the parabola $x^{2}=-3y$. The tangent to this parabola at $P$ meets the parabola $y=x^{2}$ at the points $Q$ and $R$. If the area of the region bounded by the parabola $y=x^{2}$ and the line segment $QR$ is $\dfrac{32}{3}$, then the ordinate of $P$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $P$ परवलय $x^{2}=-3y$ पर एक बिन्दु है। इस परवलय के बिन्दु $P$ पर खींची गई स्पर्श रेखा परवलय $y=x^{2}$ को बिन्दुओं $Q$ तथा $R$ पर मिलती है। यदि परवलय $y=x^{2}$ तथा रेखाखण्ड $QR$ द्वारा परिबद्ध क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल $\dfrac{32}{3}$ है, तो $P$ की कोटि ______ है।
solution: With $y=x^{2}$: $x^{2}+\dfrac{2a}{3}x-\dfrac{a^{2}}{3}=0$, $D=\dfrac{4a^{2}}{9}+\dfrac{4a^{2}}{3}=\dfrac{16a^{2}}{9}$, so the abscissae of $Q$, $R$ differ by $\dfrac{4|a|}{3}$ (needs $a\ne0$).
solution_full: Any point of $x^{2}=-3y$ is $P\left(a,-\dfrac{a^{2}}{3}\right)$. Differentiating, $2x=-3y'$, so the slope at $P$ is $-\dfrac{2a}{3}$ and the tangent is $y+\dfrac{a^{2}}{3}=-\dfrac{2a}{3}(x-a)$, i.e. $y=-\dfrac{2a}{3}x+\dfrac{a^{2}}{3}$.
For $a=0$ the tangent is $y=0$, which touches $y=x^{2}$ at one point only, so $a\ne 0$.

Intersection with $y=x^{2}$: $x^{2}+\dfrac{2a}{3}x-\dfrac{a^{2}}{3}=0$. Discriminant $D=\dfrac{4a^{2}}{9}+\dfrac{4a^{2}}{3}=\dfrac{16a^{2}}{9}>0$, so the roots $x_{1}<x_{2}$ satisfy $x_{2}-x_{1}=\sqrt D=\dfrac{4|a|}{3}$.

Between $Q$ and $R$ the chord is above the parabola, and chord minus parabola $=(x-x_{1})(x_{2}-x)$. So the area is $\displaystyle\int_{x_{1}}^{x_{2}}(x-x_{1})(x_{2}-x)dx=\dfrac{(x_{2}-x_{1})^{3}}{6}=\dfrac{1}{6}\cdot\dfrac{64|a|^{3}}{27}=\dfrac{32|a|^{3}}{81}$.
In both cases the ordinate of $P$ is $-\dfrac{a^{2}}{3}=-3$, so the answer is unique.
originality_note: New: a tangent of one parabola (x^2 = -3y) used as a chord of another parabola (y = x^2), with the cut-off area fixing the point of contact (way 5). Closest known: area between y = x^2 and a given line. Different because: the chord is defined as a tangent to a second curve, and the ratio 3 was chosen so that the discriminant is a perfect square in a.

concept_use.Area bounded by a curve and its tangent,: The tangent at P to x^2 = -3y is the chord QR of y = x^2; the area between y = x^2 and this chord is (x2 - x1)^3/6.
concept_use.Area bounded by two curves: The region is bounded by the parabola y = x^2 and the line QR, integrated as chord minus parabola.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function and curve introduced with its domain, every condition stated, one reading, answer unique and equal to the plan; Hindi mirrors the English maths. Checked a = 0 gives no chord; both a = 3 and a = -3 give ordinate -3, so the answer is unique. No change.
key_step: Write the tangent to the first parabola and use the (difference of roots)^3/6 area for the second.
justification: Two curves linked through a tangent-chord, discriminant and a cube-root step; numerical. Two ideas linked, L3, comparable to 2023-P1-Q7 (L2) plus an extra area stage.
blueprint_concepts: Area bounded by a curve and its tangent, normal or a chord
